$comment: Platform budget: the shell is what an adopter ships on day one, so its budget must survive the reference strip. Resource budgets are hard failures; lab timing metrics are warnings. See ADR 0009 for why the split exists. LIMITATION: every resource-summary assertion below is maxNumericValue -- an upper bound only. @lhci/cli 0.15.1's assertion vocabulary is exactly {minScore, maxLength, maxNumericValue} (verified against node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/assertions.js); minNumericValue does not exist, so this file cannot itself assert a resource floor, and a build that emits nothing passes every line here (0 <= any budget). That floor is enforced upstream instead: scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs's classify()/evaluate() fail loudly -- 'dist does not exist' or 'budget matched no file' -- when apps/shell/dist is missing or empty (verified by emptying it and re-running verify:bundle-size). categories:accessibility at minScore 1 is not that floor either: a syntactically valid, fully empty page (lang, viewport, title, one text node, zero scripts) scores a perfect 1.0 here, verified by request. Flagged for ADR 0009 follow-up.
